main_body: Round stone tower with a green conical tile roof, a small window and an arched wooden door
top_band: Green tiled cone roof rows 3-39, light mint at left through mid green to dark teal at right, with a dark green eave row at 38-40 and a brown eave line at 40-41
evidence: Reading down the centre column: the roof slope is a large visible tile surface (about 36 rows) that ends in a brown eave line (rows 40-41) with a dark teal shadow band above it. Below that is the stone front face, about 52 rows. The window has a frame, a sill with planter and a dark inner top edge. The door is set in a stone surround with an arched top. The roof slope is the top surface, as in the reference houses, so the drawing reads as 3/4. The wall itself is a plain front face, but the roof and eave carry the top.

style.evidence: The roof has about 5 greens with scallop tile rows, and the outline is a dark tinted green or grey-violet, not black, which matches the Beodeul approach. The stone wall is weaker: bricks are mostly 2-3 flat greys with big flat blocks of one colour (about 8x4 px and larger) and no grain or per-stone speckle, while the references have rich per-tile shading and plaster or stone texture. The wall tiles and the door panel are mostly 3-4 colours, so the piece is thinner than the references. Strictly, it falls short of the Beodeul bar.
